newsitem.title: TURKEY: Istanbul gold trade sinks as market enters holiday.
newsitem.headline: Istanbul gold trade sinks as market enters holiday.

text.p: Volume on the Istanbul gold exchange plunged to 115 kilos from Wednesday's 1,751 kilos in subdued trade as the market started a four and a half day religious holiday, dealers said.
Gold prices ended firmer at $342.65 an ounce versus $340.50 at Wednesday's close, in line with higher Europoean levels. There were no lira deals. Wednesday's lira close was 1,457,200 lira per gram.
The exchange will open on April 22 but will close again for a national holiday on April 23 and resume trade on April 24.

Dealers do not expect much activity on April 22 when financial and capital markets will be closed. Money, bond, foreign exchange and stock markets closed at midday Thursday and will reopen on April 24.
